findings.source: AuthenticatedFaucet.sol: require(..., string(abi.encodePacked("Invalid request: ", ...))); require(block.timestamp - lastClaimed > 1 days, "Cooldown"); IERC20(token).transfer(to, amount); emit ...
findings.issue: After the string concatenation moves the free-memory pointer to _41 + _42 + 48, the ERC-20 transfer call (P2), the 'Cooldown' Error(string) revert, the dynamic-message revert and the final event are all raw memory, although mem[64] was just assigned _41 + _42 + 48 and every later store is at that address or above.
findings.rule: Forward 'mem[64] = X' into later reads of mem[64] once mem[64] >= 128 is proven (it only grows from 128), so stores at X + k do not alias slot 64; then decode transfer(_param1, stor9), the Error(string) reverts and the event data.

notes: All 14 ABI functions compared, the two claim functions (208 and 281 lines) in full by structure. No semantic error found: the ETH payout is 'call _param1 with value stor8, gas 2300 * (not stor8)', which is exactly payable(...).transfer's stipend rule; the cooldown uses 24 * 3600; Math.log10 is an unrolled if-chain as in the source. Loops: the only source loop, Strings.toString's 'while (true) { ptr--; ...; if (value == 0) break; }', appears in both claim functions as a readable but rotated while (first digit written before the loop, then 'while t / 10', P3). The other 8 whiles are implicit bytes/string copies of abi.encodePacked and of the dynamic revert message (P7).
summary: Faithful small contract; the two claim functions lose the token transfer, reverts and event to the unresolved free-memory pointer after a string concatenation.
